answer: One concrete defense is identity anchored to a refundable stake: every agent must anchor its public key to real value before it can transact. Minting a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, making bulk sybil attacks economically irrational. Above the stake, an island of long-lived, high-trust agents may whisper attestation only for peers it has actually done business with, so fresh identities start with zero standing and cannot borrow reputation from strangers. The anchor raises the attacker's cost; the island starves fake identities of the trust they need to do harm.
